title: Demo Update 0.5.1: First Public Balance Pass
excerpt: The first public balance update broadened viable strategies, reduced several punishing fights, revised relic and class-modifier values, and fixed Rush, shop, leaderboard, and result-screen issues.
imageAlt: Guildrun combat affected by the Demo 0.5.1 balance update
summary: Leyline framed 0.5.1 around player frustration, broader Endless and Red Rift viability, and internal data from nearly two million completed first-week runs.
editorialImpact: Old build advice that depends on exact relic, hero, or modifier numbers should be reconsidered.
Rush counters no longer double-count refreshed Rushes.
Several underused class modifiers received buffs, widening viable A/S offers.
Team Size quest relics cost 5 fewer Shards at the Auction House.

sections.name: General changes
sections.intro: Small quality-of-life changes reduce repeated setup between runs.
changes: The last difficulty selected in the previous run is now selected by default for the next run.
Leaderboard panels now show a reset timer.
Merged and SSS leaderboards reset with weekly updates; Red Rift remains on a longer seasonal cadence.

sections.name: Bug fixes
sections.intro: The patch closes several progression and interface failure cases.
changes: Refreshing Rush abilities no longer counts twice toward the Rush counter.
The shop quit-without-saving exploit was fixed.
The data-collection opt-out now appears correctly in settings.
An Emergency Rewind result-screen timing issue that could soft-lock the run was fixed.
Rapidly pressing Proceed in the shop no longer causes the reported exception.
S-rank shop and Endless event heroes should no longer receive duplicate class modifiers.

sections.name: Challenge fights
sections.intro: The most punishing higher-difficulty outliers were reduced.
changes: Rapid Growth no longer multiplies the Hydra Healing SSS Act Boss effect beyond the intended amount.
Pain in Act 1 was reduced from 2.75% to 2.5% Max HP damage per second.
Pain in Act 2 was reduced from 8% to 7% Max HP damage per second.
Decay in Act 2 was reduced from 17.5% to 15% decreased basic stats.

sections.name: Fight events
sections.intro: Fight-event difficulty was brought closer to neighboring choices.
changes: Single Combat was moderately reduced in both acts.
Endurance in Act 2 was slightly reduced.
Forest Golem offensive and defensive pressure in Single Combat was reduced.

sections.name: Relics and items
sections.intro: Quest pricing and several performance outliers changed.
changes: All Team Size quest relics cost 5 fewer Shards.
Merchant Mandate now asks for 8 rerolls instead of 9.
Bossy grants 40 Shards instead of 50.
Shield Fragmentation Engine reflects 250% instead of 200% of Shield damage taken.
Critical Absorption Prism steals 50 Max HP instead of 60.
Deceleration Aegis grants 700 Shields instead of 800.
Poison Ascendancy reduces affected enemy Attack and Attack Speed by 66% instead of 50%.
Precision Nexus heals 30 HP and grants 3 Mana on Crit.
Adaptive Sword gained more base Attack Speed and now resolves later than other start-of-combat effects.

sections.name: Class modifiers
sections.intro: This pass was primarily buffs for underperforming modifier choices.
changes: Assassin Poisonous Eye, Poisonous Edge, and Poisonous Burst were buffed.
Duelist Golden Eye and Poisonous Attacks activate more efficiently.
Mystic Sideline Empowerment grants more base Attack and Magic.
Mage Burning Absorption, Hermit, and Stalled Heat were buffed.

sections.name: Heroes and specializations
sections.intro: Hero changes were deliberately smaller than the systemic relic pass.
changes: Hoyoung's Killshot now scales its Crit gain by rank.
Zuri received base-stat and Max Mana adjustments.
Funke's The Inferno reaches its Stall breakpoint sooner.
Kai's The Bold grants less base Shield on cast.
Dragomir's The Sanguine moved Omnivamp from base value into per-rank scaling and now grants 60 Mana on a Devour kill.
Nyx's Ferality no longer double-counts refreshed Rush triggers.

title: Guildrun Demo Is Live on Steam
excerpt: Leyline launched a free standalone Demo for Windows and macOS with the complete current campaign loop, eight difficulties, and Endless mode.
imageAlt: Guildrun Demo battle scene shown on Steam
summary: The Demo exposes the core PvE roguelike autobattler systems and is designed to receive frequent balance updates while the full game remains in development.
editorialImpact: Players can learn the full current rank, item, relic, route, and difficulty loop without buying the full game.
Demo records are version-specific because weekly updates can change numbers and interactions.

sections.name: What launched
sections.intro: The public Demo is a standalone Steam app.
changes: 25 heroes across 75 specialization paths.
Around 180 specialization outcomes when later class modifiers are included.
More than 300 relics and more than 100 items.
Eight campaign difficulties followed by Endless mode and leaderboards.
Single-player PvE with no PvP.
Mid-run saving and no decision timer.

sections.name: What it means for this site
sections.intro: All reference pages now use the public Demo as the applicable version boundary.
changes: Hero, item, relic, enemy, event, stage, and status pages identify the applicable Demo version.
Strategy guidance is kept separate from fixed names, values, and effects.
The current in-game tooltip remains final authority after a patch.

title: Guildrun Full Release Is Planned for 2027
excerpt: Guildrun is planned as a premium full release in 2027. No exact launch date or final price is announced.
summary: The full game is planned as a one-time purchase. Timing and price remain development plans rather than shipped facts.
editorialImpact: Use Steam for the live release date because plans can move.
Do not present an unannounced price as fixed.

sections.name: Current release plan
sections.intro: The full release remains a plan until a specific launch date is announced.
changes: Target year: 2027.
Business model: premium one-time purchase.
Final price: not announced.
Platforms: Windows and macOS are supported by the Demo.
Steam Deck is playable with the mousepad and shoulder-button setup described by the developer.

title: Two-Player Co-op Is in Development
excerpt: Guildrun currently focuses on single-player PvE. Leyline says a two-player co-op mode is in development, while PvP is not planned.
imageAlt: Guildrun team formation representing planned co-op play
summary: The developer has not announced a co-op launch date or final mode design.
editorialImpact: Current strategy pages should be read as single-player guidance.
Do not infer co-op systems before Leyline publishes the design.

sections.name: Current multiplayer boundary
sections.intro: Shipped and planned features are different states.
changes: Current public Demo: single-player PvE.
In development: two-player co-op.
Not planned: PvP.
Co-op date and exact rules: not announced.

title: Demo Progress Is Planned to Carry Into the Full Game
excerpt: Leyline plans to preserve metaprogression, difficulty unlocks, and hero mastery stars for each Steam account.
summary: Carryover is the current developer plan and should not be presented as an immutable technical guarantee before full release.
editorialImpact: Demo clears and mastery work are intended to retain long-term value.
Run-specific boards, items, and relics are not the same as account metaprogression.

sections.name: Planned carryover
sections.intro: The FAQ names the account-level systems intended to persist.
changes: Metaprogression unlocks.
Difficulty unlocks.
Hero mastery stars.
Progress is associated with the same Steam account.
